[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant provided a list of materials needed for a freestanding tub and a large walk-in shower, including:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - Freestanding tub: acrylic, cast iron, or solid surface; costs between $1,000 to $3,000.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - Tub feet or pedestal: prices range from $100 to $500.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - Tub filler or faucet: prices between $200 to $1,000.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - Tub surround: prices vary widely depending on material and size.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - Shower pan or base: prices range from $500 to $2,000.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - Shower walls: options include tile, glass, or acrylic; prices vary.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - Shower door or enclosure: prices range from $500 to $2,000.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - Showerhead and handheld shower: prices range from $100 to $500.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - Drain and linear drain: prices range from $100 to $500.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant provided additional materials needed, including flooring, walls, plumbing, electrical, tile, and grout.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant advised to hire professionals for tasks beyond user’s expertise and to ensure the bathroom's floor can support the weight of the freestanding tub.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant provided tips for a successful tile installation.  
[PREFERENCE] User is thinking of using porcelain tile for the shower walls and floor.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant recommended both glazed and unglazed porcelain tile, explaining the differences:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - Glazed porcelain tile has a glossy finish, is more durable, easier to clean, and highly resistant to water.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - Unglazed porcelain tile has a natural look, increased grip, and is less expensive but may require more maintenance.  
[PREFERENCE] User prefers glazed porcelain tile for the shower walls and floor due to the glossy finish and added
